entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Fox Film Corporation, founded in 1915 by William Fox, was one of Hollywood's original major studios and the predecessor to 20th Century Fox. Fox Film Corporation pioneered talking pictures technology, sound newsreels (the Fox Movietone News), and widescreen CinemaScope. William Fox's attempt to acquire MGM in 1929 — which would have created Hollywood's dominant studio — was blocked by the US government, leading to his bankruptcy in the 1930s and the studio's merger with Darryl F. Zanuck's Twentieth Century Pictures.

William Fox, a Jewish immigrant from Hungary, started in penny arcades and film distribution before establishing Fox Film Corporation. Fox's development of Movietone sound-on-film technology (as opposed to Warners' sound-on-disc Vitaphone) became the industry standard for sound films. Fox Movietone News (1927-1963) provided the primary source of filmed news content for American cinema audiences before television.

The 1935 merger creating 20th Century-Fox under Darryl F. Zanuck produced a studio that became one of Hollywood's 'Big Five.' Fox's history from Zanuck through the Murdoch acquisition (1985), Alien, Die Hard, Star Wars' special effects work, and Avatar demonstrates American cinema's corporate evolution. The 2019 Disney acquisition of 20th Century Fox (for $71.3 billion) ended the studio's 85-year independent existence, making Fox's assets part of Disney's entertainment empire.
